html:
Gauss's law box for a wave
1. The Gaussian box
A teal box of face area l × l and thickness Δx straddles the x-axis, the direction the wave travels. Identical red field triads are drawn at x and at x+Δx.
Electric flux through each face
Side 3 (x, −x̂): Φ = −Ex(x,t)·l²
Side 4 (x+Δx, +x̂): Φ = +Ex(x+Δx,t)·l²
Side 2 (top, +ŷ): Φ = +Ey·Δx·l
Side 1 (bottom, −ŷ): Φ = −Ey·Δx·l
z-faces (±ẑ): Φ = ±Ez·Δx·l
l² = 9.00, Δx·l = 3.60
Φnet = [Ex(x+Δx,t) − Ex(x,t)]·l² ≈ (∂Ex/∂x)·Δx·l²
Qenc = 0 ⇒ ∂Ex/∂x = 0
Click any face of the box to highlight it, draw its outward normal, and read its flux term. Drag to orbit.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional drawing of a translucent teal rectangular box serving as a Gaussian surface, with electric field vectors drawn at two opposite faces. A small axis key in the upper right shows y pointing up, x pointing right, and z toward the lower left. The box is tall and thin: a bracket along the left edge gives that side as l, a bracket along the top rear edge gives another side as l, and a bracket across the bottom front gives the short third dimension as Δx. Curved leaders name the faces, with Side 2 on the top, Side 1 on the bottom, Side 3 on the near left face, and Side 4 printed in gray on the face beyond. Two identical red vector triads appear, each with one arrow up, one to the right, and one toward the lower left. The left triad is labeled Ey(x,t), Ex(x,t), and Ez(x,t); the right triad, displaced by the thickness of the box, reads Ey(x+Δx,t), Ex(x+Δx,t), and Ez(x+Δx,t), and a dashed line through both origins continues to an arrowhead labeled x. Repeating one triad at two positions along x frames the comparison as flux entering one face against flux leaving the opposite one, the setup for applying Gauss's law to a wave traveling along the x-axis.

elements: Translucent teal rectangular box (Gaussian surface): thin along x, tall along y, deep along z
Dark teal edge lines on all 12 box edges (near edges solid, hidden rear edges faint)
Near-left large face (y-z plane, at x = 0) labeled 'Side 3' in black at its lower-left
Far-right large face (y-z plane, at x = Δx) labeled 'Side 4' in gray, visible facing the viewer
Top face (x-z plane, normal +y) with curved leader arrow to label 'Side 2' at upper right
Bottom face (x-z plane, normal -y) with curved leader arrow up to label 'Side 1' at lower right
Two unlabeled narrow z-normal faces (Δx × l)
Dimension bracket along the left vertical edge with label 'l' (height, y)
Dimension bracket along the top receding edge with label 'l' (depth, z)
Dimension bracket across the bottom front edge with label 'Δx' (thickness, x)
Red vector triad at x: arrow up (Ey(x,t)), arrow to the right (Ex(x,t)), arrow toward lower-left (Ez(x,t)) with italic labels
Red vector triad at x+Δx: arrow up (Ey(x+Δx,t)), arrow right (Ex(x+Δx,t)), arrow lower-left (Ez(x+Δx,t)) with italic labels
Black dashed line through both triad origins extending past the box to an arrowhead labeled 'x'
Axis key in upper right: short black arrows y up, x right, z toward lower-left with italic labels

interactions.teaches: that the figure is a closed 3D box whose six faces each have an outward normal, and that the two field triads sit on opposite faces separated only along x

interactions.label: Box thickness Δx
interactions.teaches: that Gauss's-law reasoning compares the field on two faces a small distance Δx apart along the propagation direction: as Δx shrinks, E(x+Δx,t) approaches E(x,t) and the net x-flux tends to (∂Ex/∂x)Δx·l²
which face contributes which flux term — clicking Side 1, 2, 3 or 4 highlights that face, draws its outward normal, and shows its flux expression so the learner sees which contributions cancel

interactions.label: Show Ex component
interactions.teaches: that only Ex threads the x-normal faces (Sides 3 and 4), so a non-zero net flux requires Ex to change with x

interactions.label: Show Ey component
interactions.teaches: that Ey is parallel to Sides 3 and 4 and pierces only the top/bottom faces (Sides 2 and 1), where equal-and-opposite contributions cancel

interactions.label: Show Ez component
interactions.teaches: that Ez pierces only the two narrow z-normal faces, whose contributions likewise cancel for a wave varying only with x

demo_steps.title: The Gaussian box
demo_steps.narration: A thin teal box of face area l × l and thickness Δx straddles the x-axis, the direction the wave travels. Identical red field triads are drawn at x and at x+Δx.

demo_steps.title: Only Ex crosses Sides 3 and 4
demo_steps.narration: Hiding Ey and Ez leaves only the horizontal arrows. These are perpendicular to the two large faces, so Sides 3 and 4 carry the entire electric flux: −Ex(x,t)l² entering and +Ex(x+Δx,t)l² leaving.

demo_steps.title: Ey and Ez contribute nothing net
demo_steps.narration: With only the vertical and lower-left arrows shown, the field runs parallel to the large faces and pierces the top/bottom (Sides 2, 1) and the two narrow faces in equal and opposite amounts, so those fluxes cancel.

demo_steps.title: Shrink Δx
demo_steps.narration: Narrowing the box brings the two triads together: Ex(x+Δx,t) − Ex(x,t) becomes small, and with zero enclosed charge Gauss's law forces ∂Ex/∂x = 0 — the wave has no longitudinal electric component.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Box dimensions in world units: X (screen-right, the x / propagation axis) = Δx, default 0.6, slider 0.15–1.6; Y (screen-up) = l = 3.0; Z (receding diagonal, z increasing toward lower-left as in the axis key) = l = 3.0. Box centered so its near face sits at x = 0 and its far face at x = Δx, vertical span y = −1.5…+1.5, depth z = 0…3 (near-viewer edge at z = 0 on the lower-right, receding upper-left/rear at z = 3). Viewer sits on the +x side and slightly above, so the large face at x = Δx (Side 4, gray label near its lower area) faces the viewer and the face at x = 0 (Side 3, black label at its lower-left) is the far-left panel. Side 2 = top face (y = +1.5, normal +y), curved leader from upper right; Side 1 = bottom face (y = −1.5, normal −y), curved leader from lower right; the two unlabeled Δx × l faces are the z-normal ones. Dimension brackets with tick ends: vertical 'l' just left of the x=0 face left edge; 'l' along the top receding edge of the x=0 face; 'Δx' along the bottom front edge running in x. Field triads: origin of left triad on the x = 0 face at about y = +0.1, z = 1.2; right triad at the same y,z but x = Δx. Each triad has three red arrows of length ≈0.9: +y (Ey), +x (Ex), +z i.e. screen lower-left (Ez). Black dashed line along x through both origins, extending ~1.6 beyond the right triad to an arrowhead labeled italic 'x'. Axis key at upper right: three short black arrows of length 0.5 (y up, x right, z lower-left) with italic labels. Colors: box fill translucent teal #b8dcd8 at ~0.35 opacity, edges #2f8f8c, vectors and their labels red #e8402a, most labels black #1a1a1a italic serif, 'Side 4' gray #9a9a9a, highlighted face when clicked warm yellow #f2c14e at 0.5 opacity with a white outward-normal arrow. Flux readout formulas: Side 3 flux = −Ex(x,t)·l², Side 4 flux = +Ex(x+Δx,t)·l², Sides 1/2 flux = ∓Ey·Δx·l (cancel), z-faces = ∓Ez·Δx·l (cancel); net = [Ex(x+Δx,t) − Ex(x,t)]·l² ≈ (∂Ex/∂x)Δx·l² = 0.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the box as a single BoxGeometry with MeshPhysicalMaterial (transparent, depthWrite false, side: DoubleSide) plus a LineSegments EdgesGeometry overlay for the crisp teal edges; draw hidden rear edges with a second, lower-opacity line pass so the wireframe reads like the source. Per-face highlighting: six separate thin PlaneGeometry overlays (one per face, slightly inset) used as raycast targets so clicks resolve to a named side without needing per-triangle face indexing. Vectors as ArrowHelper or custom cylinder+cone groups so shaft width stays constant; labels as CSS2DRenderer HTML spans with italic serif styling so the E-subscript notation renders cleanly and stays readable at any orbit angle. Dashed x-axis line via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Δx slider must rebuild/scale the box along X only, reposition the far face's triad, the Δx bracket, and the dimension label, and update the numeric E(x+Δx) − E(x) readout live. Component toggles fade the corresponding arrow in both triads and gray out the matching flux row in the readout panel. Keep the axis key as a small fixed HUD group that does not rotate with the orbit, matching the source's corner key.

authoredContext:
We examine first what Gauss’s law for electric fields implies about the relative directions of the electric field and the propagation direction in an electromagnetic wave. Assume the Gaussian surface to be the surface of a rectangular box whose cross-section is a square of side l and whose third side has length Δx, as shown in the figure. Because the electric field is a function only of x and t, the y-component of the electric field is the same on both the top (labeled Side 2) and bottom (labeled Side 1) of the box, so that these two contributions to the flux cancel. The corresponding argument also holds for the net flux from the z-component of the electric field through Sides 3 and 4. Any net flux through the surface therefore comes entirely from the x-component of the electric field. Because the electric field has no y- or z-dependence, Ex(x,t) is constant over the face of the box with area A and has a possibly different value Ex(x+Δx,t) that is constant over the opposite face of the box. Applying Gauss’s law gives

where A=l×l is the area of the front and back faces of the rectangular surface. But the charge enclosed is Qin=0, so this component’s net flux is also zero, and the equation implies Ex(x,t)=Ex(x+Δx,t) for any Δx. Therefore, if there is an x-component of the electric field, it cannot vary with x. A uniform field of that kind would merely be superposed artificially on the traveling wave, for example, by having a pair of parallel-charged plates. Such a component Ex(x,t) would not be part of an electromagnetic wave propagating along the x-axis; so Ex(x,t)=0 for this wave. Therefore, the only nonzero components of the electric field are Ey(x,t) and Ez(x,t), perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave.

The surface of a rectangular box of dimensions l×l×Δx is our Gaussian surface. The electric field shown is from an electromagnetic wave propagating along the x-axis.

Figure shows a rectangular box of dimensions l by l by delta x. The top and bottom sides, parallel to the xz plane are labeled side 2 and side 1 respectively. The front and back sides, parallel to the xy plane are labeled side 3 and side 4 respectively. Three arrows originate from a point on the left side. These are along the x, y and z axis and are respectively labeled E subscript x parentheses x, t parentheses, E subscript y parentheses x, t parentheses and E subscript z parentheses x, t parentheses. Three more arrows originate from the point where the x axis intersects the right side of the box. These, too, are along the the x, y and z axis and are respectively labeled E subscript x parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses, E subscript y parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses and E subscript z parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses.

A similar argument holds by substituting E for B and using Gauss’s law for magnetism instead of Gauss’s law for electric fields. This shows that the B field is also perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave. The electromagnetic wave is therefore a transverse wave, with its oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to its direction of propagation.

discrepancies: The two field triads sit almost on top of each other (separated only by Δx = 0.6 in world units), so the left and right E-label sets collide — in the source the x and x+Δx triads are drawn clearly apart with their six labels individually readable.
The whole box occupies only a small fraction of the canvas with large empty margins, so the slab reads much smaller than in the source where the box fills the frame.
'Ey(x+Δx,t)' is pushed left over the box body/edge rather than sitting to the upper-left of the right vertical arrow as in the source, and 'Side 4' (grey) is partially buried under the red arrows.
The dashed x-axis through the triads is short and barely visible; in the source it runs well past the right edge of the box with a clear arrowhead and italic x.

The original's near/far large faces are strongly shaded/translucent with distinct teal outlines; the generated fill reads paler and the hidden-edge treatment is faint, weakening the 3D slab read at small size.
evaluation.notes: Correct slab geometry, teal/red palette, full Side 1–4 / l / Δx / axis-key labelling and an unusually rich, conceptually apt interaction set (step demo, Δx slider, component toggles, clickable faces with flux terms); the main weaknesses are the cramped, mutually colliding triad labels and the small framing of the box within the canvas.
action_items: Increase the default Δx (or offset the two triads slightly in z) so the x and x+Δx triads and their six labels are visually separated as in the source.
Re-tune label offsets (especially Ey(x+Δx,t), Ex(x+Δx,t), Side 4) so no red label overlaps another label, the box edge, or an arrow shaft, and bump primary label font size for legibility.
Raise heightFraction / tighten the fit so the box and dimension brackets fill more of the canvas instead of sitting small in the upper-left region.
Extend the dashed x-axis further past the box with a larger arrowhead and place the italic 'x' clear of the Ex(x+Δx,t) label, matching the source.

A small axis key in the upper right shows y pointing up, x pointing right, and z toward the lower left. Curved leaders name the faces, with Side 2 on the top, Side 1 on the bottom, Side 3 on the near left face, and Side 4 printed in gray on the face beyond. Two identical red vector triads appear, each with one arrow up, one to the right, and one toward the lower left. The left triad is labeled Ey(x,t), Ex(x,t), and Ez(x,t); the right triad, displaced by the thickness of the box, reads Ey(x+Δx,t), Ex(x+Δx,t), and Ez(x+Δx,t), and a dashed line through both origins continues to an arrowhead labeled x. demo_steps.title: Only Ex crosses Sides 3 and 4

Each triad has three red arrows of length ≈0.9: +y (Ey), +x (Ex), +z i.e. screen lower-left (Ez). Black dashed line along x through both origins, extending ~1.6 beyond the right triad to an arrowhead labeled italic 'x'. discrepancies: Box fill reads as a desaturated grey-green in the render, while the source is a clearly teal/aqua translucent solid with saturated teal edges; the generated near-face also lacks the visible tinted overlap of the source.

Triad placement relative to the box differs: in the source the left triad is clearly inside the near half of the slab and the right triad sits on the far (x+Δx) face with the dashed x-axis running through both; in the render both triads bunch toward the right-centre so the correspondence to Sides 3 and 4 is less legible.
